newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat clarifies statement on target.
newsitem.headline: Indosat clarifies statement on target.

text.p: Indonesia telecommunications provider PT Indonesian Satellite (Indosat) issued a clarification on Wednesday regarding the company's target ahead of a government plan to allow more companies to participate in the telecommunications industry.

During an analysts' meeting last Friday, Indosat said it had set up an "intermediate target" ahead of the government's plan to allow more companies to provide international, inter-city and local call services in 2004, 2005 and 2010 respectively.
But the market interpreted the statement as an indication the government might speed up the deadline.
Indosat rose 75 rupiah on the Jakarta exchange to 6,600 rupiah on a modest turnover of 222,000 shares.
Indosat said in a statement faxed to Reuters that Friday's statement did not refer to any revision in the government policy and that it had no intention of suggesting this.
Indosat said that by 2001 it would have a strong customer base to support its position as a market leader in international business.
"In domestic business, Indosat will develop supporting businesses to create a strong domestic backbone to face the related milestones in 2005 and 2010," it said.

"The company would like to reiterate that Indosat statement made during the meeting is our internal objective to develop Indosat business towards the company's vision to become the market leader, global player and world class telecommunications operator," it said.
The government currently only allows two companies, Indosat and privately-owned PT Satelindo, partly owned by Detemobil of Deutche Telekom, to provide international calls.
Another state-controlled company Telkom has been the only one allowed to provide domestic telephone services.
Telkom fell sharply on Tuesday on investor concern over potential competition, but it recovered on Wednesday to close the day up 100 rupiah at 3,750 rupiah on a turnover of 13 million shares.
